title: DevOps and reliability
description: Review how the change ships, how the team will detect failures and how it can recover.
questions: How will the team roll out the change and detect a bad release?
Which configuration, telemetry and runbooks need updates?
Can the team roll back safely after the change has written data?

specialists.title: Release engineer
specialists.focus: Verify how the build becomes the deployed artifact. Find changes to permissions, configuration and promotion gates that affect the release.
checks: The deployed artifact is the one built and tested by the pipeline, identified by digest.
Changes to pipeline permissions, secrets or promotion gates are reviewed separately.

specialists.title: Rollout owner
specialists.focus: Choose initial exposure, a representative comparison population and the conditions for advancing, pausing or stopping the rollout.
checks: The rollout starts with a small exposure and has written advance, pause and stop conditions.
The comparison population is representative of the users who will get the change.

specialists.title: Site reliability engineer
specialists.focus: Check that service indicators surface user impact and that missing telemetry has a defined response. Confirm alert delivery and on-call ownership.
checks: Service level indicators measure user impact, and alerts reach an on-call person.
New code paths emit logs, metrics or traces that show their failures.

specialists.title: Recovery engineer
specialists.focus: Determine what persists after rollback. Check that the team can restore the service within its agreed recovery objectives.
checks: Rollback was rehearsed, and what persists after it, such as migrated data, is known.
Restore time from backup is measured against the recovery time objective.

evidence: Release revision and artifact digest, promotion path, required approvals and affected environments.
Reviewed configuration or infrastructure diff with replacement, downtime and deployment ordering risks called out.
Rollout plan with cohorts, minimum observation window and thresholds for advancing, pausing and rolling back.
Dashboard query and alert route for a critical user journey, plus an example of healthy and degraded behavior.
Recovery rehearsal with elapsed time and checks on state before and after a rollback or restore.
challenge: Who can stop this rollout, and which signal reaches them soon enough to act?
Could the first cohort look healthy because it misses a high-traffic tenant, scheduled job or slow dependency?
Which writes or external actions will survive a rollback of the deployment?
Which release step can be repeated safely if the pipeline stops after making part of the change?
decision_criteria: Promote only after the agreed observation window and signal checks pass for a representative cohort.
Pause when the team loses a required signal or cannot attribute a regression to the changed release.
Require a recovery rehearsal or an approved fallback for changes that can block restore, corrupt state or affect an irreversible operation.
Assign the deployment, rollback and on-call responsibilities before expanding exposure.
